topics.topic: Authoritative ownership of repository table names across persistence IR and emitted modules
questions: How can repository table names be held only by emitted repository modules when the same unit also says “Table names are `config.persistence` (A30)” and earlier text says the persistence closure carries them; which record or module is their one owner?

Are repository table names owned and recorded by `config.persistence`/the persistence backend IR, as the received Persistence and A30 passages say, or held only by the individual emitted repository modules as this passage says?
Which emitted module owns each table name when the persistence closure emits several repositories, stores, schema creation, foreign-key references or queries that touch more than one table?

quotes:
Table names are `config.persistence`
  (A30); the table and column layout is the persistence closure's.

`config.persistence`: the storage schema revision and table names (Factory
  `48a49aa6` … `d1280708`), carried by the persistence closure.

The storage table names of `config.persistence` are read only by the emitted repositories, through the persistence backend IR; `config.credential_hash_scheme` only by the emitted `credential_security`.
judgement.why: The authoritative record is config.persistence in the persistence closure, while emitted repositories are its runtime readers rather than independent owners.

topics.topic: Whether backend IR or the emitted module authoritatively owns deterministic values
questions: Is the authoritative owner of each value its backend IR, which necessarily records the value, or the emitted module that this sentence says holds it exclusively?
Is the backend IR the authoritative owner of each value, with the emitted module merely containing generated code, or does the emitted module own the value despite the IR also recording it?
Is the authoritative owner of such a value the backend IR or the emitted module, and which one may be edited when the value changes?

quotes: A value of a deterministic backend's IR is held only by the module emitted from it and by no constant: the media types, signatures and download names of `binary_storage` (`rules.binary_delivery_policy`), the table names of the repositories, the hashing parameters of `credential_security`.

How a read resolves a
  `file_ref` under the root and which filesystem conditions fail it is
  behaviour of the emitted `binary_storage`, not of this decision: the
  deterministic backend decides it from its IR, as for the media types
  (A14), and answers every such failure as `BinaryStorageError` (owner
  2026-11-06: current service behaviour accepted; technical decisions
  delegated).

The storage table names of `config.persistence` are read only by the emitted repositories, through the persistence backend IR; `config.credential_hash_scheme` only by the emitted `credential_security`.
judgement.why: The IR decides the generated value, while the emitted module is the sole runtime holder and reader; the passages do not authorize module-local values that differ from the IR.

topics.topic: Criterion or registry classifying code as model-written versus deterministically emitted
questions: Who owns a deployment-invariant policy value read by code that is neither classified as model-written nor emitted from a deterministic backend, and what exact criterion assigns a module to either category?

What exact registry or criterion decides whether a module is model-written or emitted from deterministic backend IR, especially for generated modules containing both emitted and model-written portions?

quotes: Every policy value model-written code reads that is the same in every deployment — a threshold, a name, a path, a closed set or a table over a State 1 enumeration — is a typed constant of `data_provider`, imported by name; no other module holds or repeats it (SPEC_STANDARD 6.10, 15.4; 2026-11-08). A value of a deterministic backend's IR is held only by the module emitted from it and by no constant: the media types, signatures and download names of `binary_storage` (`rules.binary_delivery_policy`), the table names of the repositories, the hashing parameters of `credential_security`.

Scope of the rule: the constructions a model-written module makes from its
inputs, the 74 sites of `70_record_construction_closure.json` (`SOURCE.md`
"Record construction"). Outside it, and constructing their records
themselves: the three Registry decoders of `registry_gateway` (wire decoding,
Q11); the projections of the deterministic router `api` and the viewer cookie
backend `api_irregular` (SPEC_STANDARD 6.1); and every emitted module, which
builds its records from its own backend IR — the repositories when they hydrate
rows, `credential_security` (its secret envelopes), `binary_storage`
(`BinaryPayload`) and `runtime_settings` (`RuntimeSettings`).
judgement.why: The review supplies no actual module or value that the texts leave outside both categories, so no admissible history with two observable outcomes can be built.

topics.topic: Scope and precedence of the deterministic-backend ownership exception for shared fixed values
questions: Is the list after the colon exhaustive, or does every fixed value in any deterministic backend IR—including values such as viewer-cookie attributes—belong only to its emitted module and never to `data_provider`?
Where must one release value live if both model-written code and a deterministic emitted backend directly need the same value?

quotes: A value of a deterministic backend's IR is held only by the module emitted from it and by no constant: the media types, signatures and download names of `binary_storage` (`rules.binary_delivery_policy`), the table names of the repositories, the hashing parameters of `credential_security`.

Behaviour, selection, validation, defaults, runtime configuration, or any
value a deterministic backend reads from its own IR.

What remains of `rules.http_transport_policy` — the viewer
cookie name, attributes and extraction — is IR read only by the deterministic
viewer cookie backend that `api_irregular` is emitted with
(`rules.viewer_cookie_transport_backend`); no model-written module reads it.
judgement.why: The rule applies to every value read from deterministic-backend IR, and the viewer-cookie passage expressly places its values in that category while stating that no model-written module reads them.

topics.topic: Source and scope of concrete Argon2id hashing parameters
questions: Are the concrete Argon2id hashing parameters values of deterministic backend IR, or are they the pinned hashing library's defaults fixed in source as A30 says, and does “hashing parameters” include the scheme as well as numerical library parameters?

Are concrete hashing parameters encoded in the deterministic backend IR and emitted into `credential_security`, or does `credential_security` rely on the pinned hashing library's defaults as A30 states?

A17 and the cryptographic part of A16 and A30: password hashing with
Argon2id at the library defaults (R0-06, Factory `39934597ae17`), issue of a
verification secret with the configured entropy, parsing of the
verification-secret envelope, constant-time verification, and redaction-safe
failure. The backend is `rules.credential_security_backend` (Factory

credential_hash_scheme                 = argon2id (library defaults; fixed in source, not a deployment value)

`credential_hash_scheme`: its parameters are those of the running
  service's pinned hashing library (A32), carried to States 6–7; a change
  of them is a Factory route change (A32). Owner 2026-11-06: current
  service behaviour accepted; technical decisions delegated.
judgement.why: The scheme is Argon2id and its concrete cost parameters are the pinned library's defaults, changing only through a Factory-route dependency change rather than through independently preserved numeric IR values.

topics.topic: Whether State 3 must use load_runtime_settings or may retain direct environment reads pending Route B
questions: Must code produced from this State 3 already implement the stated emitted-module behavior of calling `load_runtime_settings` at each read, or preserve the direct environment reads until a separately authorized Route B occurs?
At the State 3 handoff, must `binary_storage` call `load_runtime_settings` on every read, or is direct environment access still permitted until an unspecified future Route B?

judgement.why: This is the same unchanged question as P3: the specified emitted binary_storage calls load_runtime_settings at every read, while the direct environment access sentence records the pre-regeneration running implementation.

precedent.topic: Whether binary_storage must use load_runtime_settings immediately or retain direct environment reads
quotes: `registry_gateway` takes the Registry URL from the `registry_base_url` field of the `RuntimeSettings` that `load_runtime_settings` returns, which it calls at each Registry call: the call reads and validates the environment again through `runtime_settings`, the same environment the start validated, and no settings object is handed to the gateway or cached by it (A6, A30; owner 2026-11-09: the Registry URL is read only through `runtime_settings`, SPEC_STANDARD 6.11).

The emitted `binary_storage` takes the storage root and the read limit the same way, from the `binary_storage_root` and `binary_max_read_bytes` fields of the settings `load_runtime_settings` returns, which it calls at each binary read, and refuses that read as `BinaryStorageError` when the settings cannot be loaded (owner 2026-11-09; `binary_storage_backend` schema version 2).
precedent.why: Both modules call load_runtime_settings for each operation rather than receiving or caching the settings loaded at startup.

topics.topic: Trigger, ownership, and gating effect of initiating Route B
questions: What event requires that Route B, who owns initiating it, and may later states or code generation complete while the nonconforming adapter remains?
